info.text:
# Core Keeper

## What does this randomizer do?

Core Keeper Archipelago turns progression, crafting access, resources, and
selected discoveries into a multiworld experience. Completing enabled checks
in Core Keeper sends their placed items to the appropriate Archipelago player,
while items found by other players are delivered directly through the in-game
mod.

The default configuration randomizes the major progression needed to advance
through Core Keeper while keeping optional and high-count sanity groups
disabled. Individual crafting-station licenses, reward pools, optional checks,
sanity groups, skill experience, Death Link, and the victory goal can be
configured independently.

## What is considered a location?

Depending on the selected options, locations can include collecting materials,
opening locked chests, finding food and seeds, defeating enemies and bosses,
reaching skill levels, meeting merchants, hatching pets, catching fish, and
acquiring equipment or valuables. Disabled optional groups do not contribute
locations to the generated room.

## What items can be randomized?

Progression includes crafting-station licenses and other access required by the
chosen goal. Remaining locations are filled from the enabled physical-item,
equipment, skill-point, cache, and legendary reward pools. Received physical
items are delivered to the Core Keeper character by the client mod.

## What is the goal?

The selected goal determines the required boss chain and victory event. The
client reports completion to Archipelago when that in-game goal is completed.

tutorials.text:
# Core Keeper Multiworld Setup

This package is the evidence-validated Core Keeper Archipelago 1.1.0 release.

1. Install `core_keeper.apworld` with **Install APWorld** in the Archipelago
   Launcher, then restart Archipelago if prompted.
2. Create a Core Keeper YAML with the same slot name the player will enter in
   game, then generate and host a new room. Reusing a room generated by an
   older APWorld will not add newer locations.
3. In Core Keeper, open **Mods**, subscribe to **Core Keeper Archipelago**, and
   allow the game to restart and apply the mod.
4. From Core Keeper's main menu, open **Settings**, select **Archipelago**, and
   enter `ws://host:port` (or `wss://host:port` for a secure host), the exact
   slot name, and the optional password. Select **Save and Connect**.
5. Wait for `Saved. Connected.` before testing checks.

The APWorld and mod must be the same version. The optional PopTracker pack
should also match when it is used. The current client observes the player's
complete authoritative item buffer, including the four pouch inventory ranges
defined by the game.

The Core Keeper mod, APWorld, and tracker must be updated together. A room
generated with a different Core Keeper APWorld version is not supported.

# Core Keeper Archipelago APWorld and Tracker

Archipelago world generation, logic, PopTracker support, and the optional local
texture helper for Core Keeper Archipelago.

> **Community testing release:** Core Keeper is currently distributed as a
> custom Archipelago world. It is not included in official Archipelago builds.

## Download and install

Download the files from the
[latest release](https://github.com/URAQTDev/Core-Keeper-Archipelago-APWorld-Tracker/releases/latest):

1. Install `core_keeper.apworld` using **Install APWorld** in the Archipelago
   Launcher. This is also required before creating a Core Keeper options YAML.
2. Subscribe to **Core Keeper Archipelago** through Core Keeper's in-game
   **Mods** menu.
3. Optionally install `core_keeper_poptracker_texture_free_1.2.0-rc.2.zip` in
   PopTracker, or run `CoreKeeperArchipelago-Tracker-Setup-1.2.0-rc.2.zip` to create
   the locally textured tracker from your installed Core Keeper files.

The APWorld, mod, and tracker must use the same release version.

The tracker remains usable without Core Keeper artwork. The texture helper
creates a textured copy from the player's own installed Core Keeper files; this
repository does not redistribute extracted game artwork.

The matching in-game client mod is maintained at
[Core-Keeper-Archipelago](https://github.com/URAQTDev/Core-Keeper-Archipelago)
and is installed through Core Keeper's in-game **Mods** menu.

Current public-testing release: `1.2.0-rc.2`

## Public testing

Public playtest feedback is welcome. See [PUBLIC_TESTING.md](PUBLIC_TESTING.md)
for the requested test coverage and report format. Bugs and test reports may be
submitted through this repository's
[issues](https://github.com/URAQTDev/Core-Keeper-Archipelago-APWorld-Tracker/issues).

## AI use

This project was developed with substantial generative-AI assistance under
human direction and testing. See [AI_USE.md](AI_USE.md) for the full disclosure.

## License

Original project code and documentation are available under the MIT License.
Core Keeper and its assets belong to Pugstorm and their respective rights
holders. See `ASSET_NOTICE.md` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

For the 1.3 prerelease, follow the manual installation instructions in [RELEASE_NOTES.md](RELEASE_NOTES.md).

notes.text:
# Core Keeper Archipelago 1.1.0

## Core Rewards

Core Rewards is enabled by default for newly generated worlds. Physical AP rewards wait in a 36-slot inventory at the Core, using Core Keeper’s native chest interface. Right-click the selected Core to collect them; normal Core dialogue remains available.

The inventory accepts AP rewards only. Excess rewards queue until space becomes available, and stored rewards persist between sessions. Licenses and skill points still apply immediately. The option tooltip explains access on its own second line.

## Fixes

- Teleporting no longer sends DeathLink.
- The recipe icon cannot bypass a blocked furnace.
- Colored AP check messages fade with the game’s normal message display.
- Disabled checks no longer produce “Checked” messages or get submitted.

Use the matching 1.1.0 mod and APWorld. Existing generated worlds retain their original options; regenerate to change Core Rewards.

Known limitation: the all-checks generation test reported Purple Glowbug as unreachable in logic. This release does not claim to resolve that existing logic issue.
